findings.text: The module docstring references `purgeClears` and `purge_clears` before their declarations and before Verso is enabled, so Lean does not check those references. Fix: Move the walkthrough below the declarations with Verso enabled.

The sketch says `tableOne_run` gives the subquery rows, but its conclusion gives only fault freedom and an emptiness test. Fix: Explain that `whereOne_claims` reduces `Holds` to the truth of `NOT EXISTS` and `tableOne_run` makes that equivalent to no row satisfying the filter.

The docstring says `integer_time_clears` covers every error-free run, but the theorem assumes `env.Complete`. Fix: State that the guarantee applies to a fresh run of `sessions` in each complete environment.

The docstring says the NULL-customer purge deletes nothing, but both assertions would still pass if it deleted every row. Fix: Describe the two claim observations here and attribute row preservation to `null_customer_deletes_nothing`.

The revised sentence about a successful purge still exceeds the 25-word limit. Fix: Write “After an error-free run, the reached database contains every starting session that the purge filter did not select.”

The docstring says the effect claim changes from false to true across the purge, but the NULL-customer example starts and ends true. Fix: Limit the false-to-true statement to the integer-time and text-time examples for customer 1.

The docstring attributes the `NOT` counterexample to a NULL customer alone, but an unexpired row makes the conjunction false and `NOT` true even for a NULL customer. Fix: State that every row in `expiredSessions` is expired, so the NULL customer makes the condition NULL on every starting row.
